Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

3. Wait about 30 seconds for the phone to re-register on the network, then check the status bar again.

**Step 2 — Turn off Data Saver**
Data Saver restricts data for apps and background services, and it can cut off data entirely in some cases.

**Step 3 — Disconnect the VPN**
An active but misconfigured or stalled VPN will stop all traffic from reaching the internet and produce exactly the "No Connection" result you're seeing.
1. Open **Settings → Network & Internet → VPN**.
2. Disconnect / toggle the VPN **OFF**. (If it's a third-party VPN app, open that app and tap Disconnect.)

**Then:** run the speed test again and tell me the result.

If it works: great — you can re-enable the VPN afterward if it was working fine before; I'd leave Data Saver off unless you specifically want to conserve data.

If it still says "No Connection" with 5G and excellent signal, tell me and I'll have you try one more thing on the phone before I escalate you to technical support.

I understand the frustration — you've done everything right so far. Since signal, network mode, Data Saver and the VPN are all now clear, and your account/line are in good standing with data available, the most likely remaining cause is the **APN settings** on the phone.

APN (Access Point Name) settings are what tell your phone how to reach the carrier's data network. If they've been changed or corrupted, you can have full 5G signal and still get "No Connection" on every speed test — exactly what you're seeing.

**Step 4 — Reset your APN settings**

1. Open **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile Network → Advanced → Access Point Names**.
2. Tap the **menu (⋮)** and choose **Reset to default** / **Reset APN**.
3. Wait for the defaults to load, then **reboot the phone** — the reset will not take effect until you restart.
4. After the reboot, run the speed test again.

**Please report back with:**
- The speed test result
- Your status bar (signal + network type)

If the speed test now returns a speed (anything other than "No Connection"), we're done — and please tell me the speed so I can confirm whether it's at the level it should be on 5G.

If it still says "No Connection" after the APN reset and reboot, don't worry about troubleshooting further on your own — I'll take it from there and get you to technical support, since at that point the remaining possibilities (a line-level provisioning or SIM fault) need to be handled on our side.
